_about: The figures the panel reports do not contain. build.py reads every score and measured cost from ../ArchiveProcessor/segbench-results/; only what is below is entered by hand. Each entry says where it came from.

sonnet_api_estimate.source: The panel ran Sonnet through the subscription (claude -p), so it has no measured price. Estimate: (image tokens + prompt tokens) x $2/M input + output tokens x $10/M output, at the Claude API list price for claude-sonnet-5-5 (claude-api skill, cached 2026-10-06). Image tokens = w x h / 750 over the 99 panel images (long side 999-2400 px): mean 1,522 if the API downsizes to 1568 px / 1.15 MP, 4,505 at 2576 px / 3.75 MP. Prompt about 150 tokens (the Gemini and Qwen routes report 1,337-1,404 input tokens including the image). Output 816 tokens a page, the claude -p mean in ocr-panel-cloud.md, which may include some harness overhead. Not measured: token counting needs an API key this Mac does not have.

batch.source: OpenRouter's model catalogue (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, read 2026-10-15) lists a ':batch' variant of these models at half the standard price per input and output token. Gemini 3.8 Flash's catalogue price has risen to $0.825/$4.125 since the run, which paid $0.75/$3.75; its batch price $0.375/$1.875 is half the run's price. Mistral OCR's 50% batch discount is Mistral's own (https://mistral.ai/pricing/api/); third-party pages confirm $2 per 1,000 pages for OCR 4, not yet for 4.1. Routes not listed had no batch variant in the catalogue (DeepInfra's own batch API is 20% off, but the panel did not use it).

own_hardware.source: Routes run on our own hardware, not a paid endpoint, so they cost no money. Scores, speed and memory are read from segbench-results; only names and machines are entered here. Mac: ocr-mac-local.md (W41.mac-local-measure), mlx-community/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-4bit through mlx-vlm. FarmShare: farmshare/truth/ (cbd0e68c), Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 on vLLM 0.31.0, one L40S per run (scripts/segbench/farmshare/README.md); its cost is GPU time on Stanford's cluster.
